_about: Life web text. ripples = side-effect lines shown under a decision's result (tokens: {J} {P} {Pf} {M} {Mf} {MUM} {DAD} {SIB} {SIBr} {BF} {BFf} {JR} {OUT} {CAP} {CAPl} {PRES} {PRESl} {club}; moves also {NEWCLUB} {COUNTRY}). words = random words for {PLACE} {FOOD} etc. in scenarios. actions = free-time activities (they don't advance time). outlets = fictional media per country.

splashPrivatePartner: {Pf} hates seeing their life in the comments. She goes quiet on the phone that night.
A stranger tags {Pf} in a meme about {J}. She deletes her account for a week and doesn't say why.
{Pf}: 'Can we have one week where nobody is talking about you?' It isn't really a question.
{Pf}'s cousin screenshots the whole thing into the family group chat. {Pf} is not amused.
splashPublicPartner: {Pf} reposts it with three fire emojis. Her followers double overnight and she is glowing.
{Pf} loves the attention more than she admits. Dinner that night is a celebration.
{Pf} sends him a screenshot of her notifications: 'we're famous 😂'.
Fan accounts start calling {Pf} 'the queen of {club}'. She pretends to be embarrassed.
viralFamily: {MUM} prints out a screenshot and sticks it on the fridge, next to his school certificates.
Little {SIB} has told the whole school. Twice.
{DAD} says nothing about it on the phone, but his cousins say he showed the clip to everyone at the café.
The neighbours keep knocking on his parents' door to say they saw him on their phones.
badImageFamily: {MUM} calls, voice tight: 'People at the market are talking.' The worry costs her more sleep than him.
{DAD} sends a single message: 'Is this how we raised you?' {J} reads it ten times.
{SIB} gets teased at school about the headlines. {J} only finds out from his mother.
His grandmother asks his mother whether {J} is 'in trouble with the police'. He is not. It doesn't matter.
goodImageFamily: {MUM} forwards the article to forty people. {J} knows because thirty-nine of them message him.
{DAD} calls just to read the headline out loud. Then he hangs up. That's his way of saying he's proud.
{SIB} posts '{SIBr} of a legend 😎' on every platform there is.
imageBoard: President {PRESl} asks the media department for 'a full summary' of {J}'s week. Nobody wants to be in that meeting.
A sponsor's representative calls the club. The commercial director makes a note next to {J}'s name.
The board discuss {J} for eleven minutes at their monthly meeting. Not the good kind of eleven minutes.
imageBoardUp: The commercial department want {J} in the new shirt launch. The board like a player who sells shirts.
President {PRESl} mentions {J} by name in a speech to sponsors. That doesn't happen to everyone.
clashBacked: In the canteen, three senior players sit down next to {J} without a word. The message is clear: they've got his back.
{CAP} pulls {J} aside: 'Say less in public. But for what it's worth — you're not wrong.'
The dressing-room group chat goes suspiciously quiet whenever {Mf} posts in it.
clashIsolated: Nobody saves {J} a seat at lunch. The dressing room has picked the manager's side.
{CAP}: 'You've made it about you. That's not how it works here.' Two teammates nod along.
A teammate leaks to the press that 'some of the lads are tired of the noise around {J}'.
clashFans: The fans pick a side in the {J}–{Mf} saga, and on the forums it's loud.
A banner appears at the training ground gate the next morning. It's about {J}. It's about {Mf} too.
teachersPet: 'Coach's favourite,' someone mutters in the dressing room. Laughter. {J} pretends not to hear it.
The squad WhatsApp has a new sticker of {J}'s face on {Mf}'s body. It's funny. Mostly.
splurge: {BFf} can't stop laughing at the new purchase. 'Look at you, big shot.' The friends love it.
The old crew from home call it 'the {J} effect' — suddenly every night out is on him.
{MUM} sees the photos and asks, gently, whether he's saving anything.
windfall: For the first time in months {J} looks at his bank balance without his stomach dropping.
Money in the account. {J} sleeps through the night for the first time in weeks.
familyUp: Things are good at home, and it shows: {J} walks into training lighter.
{MUM}'s voice notes are all laughter this week. It's the best kind of medicine.
A long, easy phone call with {DAD} about nothing at all. {J} feels sixteen again, in the good way.
familyDown: The tension at home follows {J} into the training ground. He snaps at a physio and apologises.
{J} can't stop replaying the argument with {DAD}. His first touch in training goes with it.
{MUM} doesn't send her usual good-luck message. He notices the silence all day.
loveUp: {Pf} leaves a note in his kitbag: 'Go get them.' He keeps it in his locker.
A good week with {Pf}. {J} catches himself smiling in the middle of a fitness test.
{Pf} cooks his favourite and they don't talk about football once. Perfect.
powerCouplePost: {Pf} posts a photo of the two of them. The internet decides they're the cutest couple in football. Followers pour in.
Their couple photo goes viral on Indonesian Twitter. Brands start sliding into {Pf}'s DMs.
loveDown: {Pf} sleeps at her sister's place. The flat is very quiet.
The argument with {Pf} plays on a loop in his head during the tactics meeting. {Mf} has to repeat himself.
{Pf} leaves him on read. For a whole day. He checks his phone between every drill.
friendsUp: The old group chat comes alive again: memes, voice notes, insults. {J} laughs until he cries.
{BFf} sends him a photo from their school days. Muddy pitch, borrowed boots. It resets everything.
A night with real friends who don't care about his stats. Exactly what he needed.
friendsDown: {BFf}'s messages get shorter. Then they stop. {J} notices on a Sunday, alone.
The group chat has moved on without him. Inside jokes he doesn't understand anymore.
friendLeak: Someone from {J}'s old circle has been talking to {JR}. A 'source close to the player' appears in {OUT}.
A blurry photo of {J} from a private party ends up on a gossip account. Only friends were there.
fansUp: The supporters' club vote {J} their player of the month. The board notice the shirt sales.
A new chant. It's about {J}. It's terrible, it doesn't rhyme, and it's the best thing he's ever heard.
Kids at the training-ground gate are wearing his number now.
fansDown: Every touch from {J} is greeted with a groan now. You can hear it from the bench.
The fan podcast spend twenty minutes on 'the {J} problem'. He listens to four of them.
dressingTalk: What's said in the dressing room reaches {Mf}'s office by Friday. It always does.
{CAP} has a word with the coaching staff. {J}'s name comes up.
dressingRespect: {CAP} mentions {J} to {Mf}: 'The lads trust him.' It counts for a lot.
The senior players have started including {J} in the leadership chats. {Mf} notices.
pressUp: {JR} at {OUT} writes a glowing piece. Other papers copy whole paragraphs.
The media like {J} now. The questions get softer, the headlines kinder.
pressHit: {OUT} runs it on the back page with an unflattering photo. {MUM} sees it first.
The tone of the coverage turns. 'Talented, but…' is how every article starts now.
{JR} writes a column titled 'What is going on with {J}?'. It is shared widely.
boardPressure: President {PRESl} has a word with {Mf}. Nobody hears what was said. Everybody can guess.
The board want 'clarity' on {J}. {Mf} is the one who has to provide it.
boardHappy: President {PRESl} shakes {J}'s hand in the corridor and remembers his name. {Mf} sees it.
The board are pleased. A word from upstairs makes {Mf}'s life easier.
restStress: Proper rest. The knot in {J}'s shoulders finally lets go.
Ten hours of sleep and a slow breakfast. The world feels smaller and more manageable.
tiredStress: His legs are heavy and his mind is heavier. The fatigue is starting to talk.
Exhaustion makes everything look worse. {J} knows it, and it doesn't help.
stressSpill: {J} brings the pressure home. {Pf} gets the short answers and the closed door.
{Pf}: 'You're here, but you're not here.' She's right.
badMoodHome: The mood follows him through the front door. Nobody at home deserves it.
{J} drives home in silence and stays in the car for twenty minutes before going in.
goodMood: There's a bounce in his step. Even the kit man notices.
{J} hums in the shower after training. The physios exchange a look.
moveAbroad: The move to {COUNTRY} means saying goodbye to everyone. {MUM} cries at the airport. {BFf} pretends he doesn't.
A new country, a new language, a new loneliness. {DAD} says, 'Make us proud.' The group chat says, 'Don't forget us.'
moveAbroadPartner: {Pf} has to decide whether to follow him to {COUNTRY}. The conversation goes on until 3am and ends without an answer.
Long distance with {Pf} starts tonight: video calls across time zones and a lot of 'are you awake?'
moveDomestic: A new city, same country. {MUM} has already found the cheapest bus route to visit him.
Moving to {NEWCLUB} means new streets, new faces, and old friends slightly further away.

PLACE: a quiet café near the training ground
the mall on the edge of town
a noodle stall under a flyover
FOOD: a giant plate of fried chicken
a protein shake that tastes like chalk
pizza nobody should be eating in season
a smoothie bowl the nutritionist approved
CAR: a hybrid the club gave him
SHOW: an old cartoon from his childhood
a football documentary about a club he hates
GIFT: a bouquet the size of a small child
WEATHER: a cold wind off the sea
fog so thick the far goal disappears

actions.label: Call home
actions.desc: An hour on the phone with family.

text: {MUM} talks for forty minutes about the neighbours' goat, a wedding, and whether he's eating vegetables. He feels human again.
{DAD} picks up, says 'Good, good,' four times, and then passes the phone to {MUM}. Classic. Perfect.
Little {SIB} hijacks the call to show him a new trick with a ball. It's terrible. He tells them it's amazing.
The call starts nicely and ends in an argument about money, as calls with {DAD} sometimes do.
{MUM} cries a little on the phone. She says she's fine. He doesn't sleep well.

actions.label: Date night
actions.desc: Switch off football. Take {Pf} out.

text: Dinner at {PLACE}. No phones, no football talk. {Pf} laughs at a joke he didn't know was funny.
They cook together and burn the rice. It's the best evening in weeks.
A long drive with no destination and all of {Pf}'s favourite songs. He knows every word now.
A fan asks for a selfie mid-dinner. Then another. Then a queue. {Pf} eats dessert alone.
A photographer catches them leaving {PLACE}. The photo is everywhere by morning.

actions.label: Say yes to a blind date
actions.desc: A friend knows someone. 'Trust me.'

text: Coffee turns into dinner turns into a three-hour walk. Her name is {P}. He texts her before he's even home.
She spends the whole evening asking about other footballers. {J} pays the bill and goes home.
Nice person, zero spark. They agree to be friends and both mean it.
She posts a photo of the date before dessert arrives. The comments are a war zone.

actions.label: Hang out with {BFf}
actions.desc: Your best friend, {BFjob}. Knows you from before.

text: They eat {FOOD} and argue about nothing for three hours. {BFf} doesn't ask about football once. Bliss.
{BFf} drags him to the old pitch behind the school. They play one-on-one until it's dark. {BFf} still cheats.
Mopeds, midnight, {FOOD} from the same stall as when they were fourteen.
{BFf} needs to borrow money for his mother's medicine. {J} doesn't hesitate.

actions.label: Video call the old crew
actions.desc: {BFf} and the gang, across the time zones.

text: Six faces on a cracked screen, everyone talking at once. {BFf} has dyed his hair orange. Nobody knows why.
They make him show them his new apartment. They are deeply unimpressed by the view and very impressed by the fridge.
Only {BFf} turns up. The others 'are busy'. It stings more than it should.

actions.label: Team night out
actions.desc: Bowling and dinner with the squad.

text: Bowling. {CAPl} is shockingly good. {J} is shockingly bad. The squad will mention this for a month.
A long dinner where the veterans tell stories about managers past. {J} laughs until his ribs hurt.
Someone posts a video from the night. It's harmless. The comments are not.
The night goes on too late. Training the next morning is a blurry nightmare.

actions.label: Post on {APP}
actions.desc: Give the fans something.

text: A training-ground photo with a caption about hard work. It does numbers.
A throwback picture of himself aged eight in a shirt three sizes too big. The internet melts.
A clip of him juggling a lemon in the kitchen. It is inexplicably his most-liked post ever.
A cryptic caption — 'some people will see' — is read as a dig at {Mf}. It wasn't. It doesn't matter.
An old tweet of his from age fourteen resurfaces in the replies. It's very bad. Mostly spelling.

actions.label: Stream a game night
actions.desc: Go live and play with fans.

text: Three hours live. He loses every match and roasts himself the whole time. Chat loves him.
A teammate joins the stream uninvited. The chemistry is chaos. The clips go everywhere.
He rage-quits on stream and says something about the referee from last week. The league is watching too.
A troll spams the chat with his family's address. He ends the stream shaking.

actions.label: Video session with the analyst
actions.desc: Two hours of clips: your last match, frame by frame.

text: The analyst pauses on one moment forty times. By the end, {J} sees the pitch differently.
They go through every one of his touches. It's humbling. It's useful.
{Mf} walks in halfway through, raises an eyebrow, and sits down to watch with them. That's new.

actions.label: Extra gym session
actions.desc: Push the body further.

text: An extra hour of squats and sprint drills after everyone's gone home.
Plyometrics until his legs shake. The fitness coach nods approvingly from the doorway.
A tweak in the hamstring on the last set. Probably nothing. Probably.

actions.label: Knock on {Mf}'s door
actions.desc: Ask what you need to do to play more.

text: {Mf} talks for twenty minutes about pressing triggers. {J} takes notes. The door stays open after that.
'You want to play? Good. That's the right question.' A short, useful conversation.
{Mf} is busy and irritated. 'Not now.' It feels worse than a no.
{Mf} listens, then says, 'You'll play when you deserve it.' The meeting lasts ninety seconds.

actions.label: Coffee with {JR}
actions.desc: Off the record with the {OUT} reporter.

text: {JR} is easy company. Off the record means off the record. A friend in the press is worth a lot.
They talk about their hometowns. {JR} writes a kind line about him the next week.
One 'off the record' sentence appears in {OUT} on Saturday, attributed to 'a source close to the player'.

actions.label: Visit a children's hospital
actions.desc: Signed shirts and an afternoon with the kids.

text: A boy with a shaved head asks him to sign his cast and then critiques his finishing. {J} has never been so happy to be insulted.
The children's ward chant his name. A nurse cries. {J} sits in the car afterwards for a long time.
The club's media team film everything. It feels less like a visit and more like content. He says so. They don't like that.

actions.label: Full day of rest
actions.desc: Sleep, {SHOW}, nothing.

text: Eleven hours of sleep and three episodes of {SHOW}. The body says thank you.
He switches off his phone at noon. By evening, he can't remember why he was stressed.
He tries to rest but scrolls through criticism for three hours instead. Not rest.

actions.label: Send money home
actions.desc: Help with the bills.

text: {MUM} sends a voice note that is mostly crying and a little bit scolding. 'You need it more than us!' They need it more.
The roof gets fixed. {DAD} sends a photo of it, no caption.
Word gets around the extended family. Three uncles call the same week, all with 'opportunities'.

actions.label: Explore the city
actions.desc: Get to know your new home.

text: He gets lost on purpose and finds a tiny restaurant that cooks almost like home. He'll be back.
A walk by the river. An old man playing chess beats him in nine moves and gives him a lesson for free.
Locals recognise him and a crowd forms. He spends the afternoon signing receipts.

actions.label: Language lesson
actions.desc: Learn the dressing-room language.

text: Verbs, verbs, verbs. He tries a joke in the dressing room the next day. Half of them laugh. Progress.
His teacher makes him order lunch in the language. He gets chicken instead of fish. Close enough.

actions.label: Fan signing session
actions.desc: An hour at the club shop.

text: A queue out the door. An old man shows him a photo of himself at the club's first-ever match. A kid asks him to sign his forehead.
Two hundred signatures and a hand cramp. Worth every one.
Only eleven people turn up. One of them wanted the other player.

actions.label: Quiet time alone
actions.desc: Prayer, a walk, a notebook. Just think.

text: An hour alone with his thoughts. He writes down three things he's grateful for and one thing he's afraid of.
He sits by the window until the city goes dark. Some weeks, that's the most important training session.

actions.label: Time for a hobby
actions.desc: {HOBBY}. Something that isn't football.

text: An evening of {HOBBY}. He is bad at it, and being bad at something without an audience feels wonderful.
{HOBBY}, two hours, no phone. He's improving. Slowly. Like everything that matters.
He posts a clip of himself {HOBBY}. The comments are delighted. A brand gets in touch.
